questions.question: Who was the first chairman of the Finance Commission of India?
questions.solution: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951, and its Chairman was K.C. Neogy.

questions.question: Under which of the following Acts was the National Commission for Women established?
questions.option_1: The National Commission for Women Act, 1988
questions.option_2: The National Commission for Women Act, 1990
questions.option_3: The National Commission for Women Act, 1989
questions.option_4: The National Commission for Women Act, 1987
questions.solution: The National Commission for Women (NCW) is a statutory body established in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.

questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for attending to disputes concerning recruitment and conditions of service of public personnel at the Centre?
questions.solution: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) was established under Article 323A (added by the 42nd Amendment) and the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, to adjudicate disputes regarding the recruitment and service conditions of persons appointed to public services of the Union.

questions.question: Who conducts elections for both the houses of Parliament in India?
questions.solution: Under Article 324, the Election Commission of India is responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to the Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.question: In India, which Ministry issues the coins of all denominations?
questions.solution: While the RBI issues currency notes (except ₹1), the Ministry of Finance has the sole right to mint coins of all denominations under the Coinage Act, 2011. The ₹1 note is also issued by the Ministry of Finance and bears the signature of the Finance Secretary.

questions.question: The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission can be removed by the order of the __________.
questions.solution: This is a critical point: although the Governor appoints the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission (SPSC), they can only be removed by the President of India (under Article 317) on grounds of misbehavior after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Constitutional Body in India?
questions.option_4: Union Public Service Commission of India
questions.solution: The State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) is a statutory body created under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The others (ECI, SPSC, UPSC) are specifically mentioned in the Constitution and are therefore constitutional bodies.

questions.question: In which year did the Election Commission of India for the first time in its history become a multi-member body?
questions.solution: From 1950 to 1989, the ECI was a single-member body. On October 16, 1989, the President appointed two more commissioners to handle the increased work due to the reduction of the voting age from 21 to 18.

questions.question: The Gram Sabha is a meeting of all adults who live in the area covered by a __________.
questions.solution: A Gram Sabha is the smallest and primary unit of the Panchayati Raj system. It consists of all persons whose names are included in the electoral rolls for the Panchayat at the village level.

questions.question: The Bureau of Indian Standard (BIS) is a statutory body working under the aegis of which union ministry?
questions.option_2: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
questions.option_4: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
questions.solution: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is the national standards body of India, established under the BIS Act, 2016. It operates under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the objectives of the NITI Aayog?
questions.option_1: To develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level
questions.option_2: To design and print new currency notes and to bring them in circulation
questions.option_3: To pay special attention to the sections of our society that may be at risk of not benefiting adequately from economic progress.
questions.option_4: To evolve a shared vision of national development priorities.
questions.solution: The RBI (Reserve Bank of India) is responsible for designing, printing, and circulating currency notes. NITI Aayog is a policy think-tank focused on cooperative federalism and economic planning.

questions.question: The State Finance Commission is appointed every_____ years by the_______
questions.solution: Under Article 243-I, the Governor of a state (state government authority) is required to constitute a Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of the Panchayats.

questions.question: What is the tenure of the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission?
questions.solution: Following the 2019 amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act, the tenure of the Chairperson and members of the NHRC was reduced from 5 years to 3 years (or until the age of 70, whichever is earlier).

questions.question: In which year was a new Constitution adopted in Sri Lanka creating the 'Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka'?
questions.solution: Sri Lanka adopted its second republican constitution on September 7, 1978, which introduced an executive presidential system and officially named the country the 'Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka'.

questions.question: In which year did Nepal adopt its first democratic constitution?
questions.solution: After years of transition from a monarchy to a republic, Nepal officially adopted its first democratic and federal constitution on September 20, 2015.

questions.question: Which principle of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ensures that entities collecting personal data must obtain explicit consent from individuals?
questions.solution: The Notice and Choice Framework requires data fiduciaries to give clear notice to individuals about what data is collected and for what purpose, ensuring that the individual has the 'choice' to provide informed explicit consent.

questions.question: Which of these is not a feature of Indian federalism?
questions.solution: Indian federalism is 'quasi-federal'. While it has a written constitution and division of powers, it features Single Citizenship (one citizenship for the whole of India). Dual citizenship is a feature of federalism in countries like the USA.

questions.question: What is the punishment for abetment of an offense under the POCSO Act?
questions.option_2: Half the punishment prescribed for the offense
questions.solution: Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, Sections 16 and 17 state that anyone who abets (encourages or assists) a crime under the Act shall be punished with the same punishment provided for that specific offense.

questions.question: If "a soldier fires on a mob by the order of his superior officer, in conformity with the law", has he committed an offence according to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
questions.option_1: Yes, because he could have disobeyed
questions.option_3: No, because he followed public orders
questions.option_4: No, because he believed in good faith that he was bound by law
questions.solution: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, an act is not an offence if it is done by a person who, by reason of a mistake of fact and not by reason of a mistake of law, in good faith believes himself to be bound by law to do it. A soldier firing on a mob under a lawful order is protected from liability.

questions.question:
Identify the following constitutional attributes with their respective democratic values:
Column A (Attribute): a) Fundamental Duties, b) Equal voting rights, c) Local self-government, d) Religious freedom
Column B (Value): i. Grassroots democracy, ii. Respect for individual conscience, iii. Recognition of citizens' responsibilities, iv. Principle of universal franchise
questions.solution:
a-iii: Fundamental Duties represent citizen responsibilities.
b-iv: Equal voting rights represent the Universal Adult Franchise.
c-i: Local self-government (Panchayats) is the essence of grassroots democracy.
d-ii: Religious freedom protects individual conscience.

questions.question: Under which ministry does the National Productivity Council (NPC) operate?
questions.option_3: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
questions.solution: The National Productivity Council (NPC) is an autonomous body under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), which falls under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Land and agriculture fall under the State List.
Statement II: Marriage laws and adoption fall under the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.option_3: Both statements I and II are correct
questions.option_4: Neither statement I nor II is correct
questions.solution: Under the 7th Schedule of the Indian Constitution, Land and Agriculture are items in the State List (List II). Marriage, divorce, and adoption are items in the Concurrent List (List III), meaning both the Centre and States can legislate on them.

questions.question: The new criminal laws (BNS, BNSS, BSA) aim to replace British-era laws with a focus on:
questions.solution: The primary objective of the 2023 criminal law reforms (replacing IPC, CrPC, and IEA) is to shift the focus from 'punishment' to 'justice delivery' and to protect the fundamental rights of citizens in a modern context.

questions.question: Under Chapter V of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which of the following qualifies as primary evidence?
questions.option_1: A counterpart document executed by one of the parties
questions.option_2: A photocopy of the document signed by a clerk
questions.option_4: A typed copy of the original document
questions.solution: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), primary evidence means the document itself. When a document is executed in counterparts (each party signing a copy), each counterpart is considered primary evidence against the party who signed/executed it.

questions.question: What is the maximum time limit for completing the trial of a case under the POCSO Act?
questions.solution: The POCSO Act, 2012, mandates that trials for sexual offences against children should be completed within one year from the date of taking cognizance by the Court to ensure swift justice and minimize trauma.
